title: What does your burnout look like?
intro: Burnout doesn't always mean completely falling apart. Sometimes it looks like losing motivation, feeling emotionally flat, or struggling to recover even after rest. This check-in is designed to help you recognize how burnout may currently be affecting you emotionally, mentally, and physically.

options.text: Physically and mentally exhausted but still functioning
Disconnected from motivation or emotions
Guilty when I try to slow down
Overwhelmed by how much I take on
Emotionally drained from constantly supporting others

questions.text: When responsibilities build up, I usually:

options.text: Continue pushing through exhaustion
Mentally check out or feel detached
Force myself to keep going no matter what
Say yes to more than I can realistically handle
Prioritize everyone else before myself
Rest doesn't fully recharge me anymore
Things I used to care about feel harder to connect with
I don't know how to fully stop or rest
Too many people rely on me emotionally
I have very little energy left for myself

questions.text: People around me probably see me as:

options.text: Hardworking and productive
Quieter or less emotionally engaged lately
Constantly busy
Dependable and always available
Supportive to everyone around me

questions.text: What do you need most right now?

options.text: Real recovery time
Emotional reconnection
Permission to slow down
Stronger boundaries and balance
Support for yourself too

a.description: You continue functioning and staying productive despite deep exhaustion. You show up every day — but your body and mind are asking for real rest.

b.description: You feel emotionally disconnected, flat, or detached from things you normally care about. This is your nervous system's way of protecting you from overload.

c.description: You feel guilty slowing down and constantly push through stress or exhaustion. Rest feels unearned — but your nervous system needs it more than you know.

d.description: You take on too much responsibility and struggle setting limits with others. Your generosity is real — but it's costing you more than you can afford right now.

e.description: You spend most of your emotional energy supporting others while neglecting your own recovery. You give so much — it's time to receive some support too.
